data.reasoning: The disagreement stems from a tool error in Report 1 (HTTP 400 when reviewing PKGBUILD in detail), not from substantive security concerns. Report 1's initial PKGBUILD audit succeeded and found no dangerous top-level code. Report 2 successfully completed the detailed PKGBUILD review, confirming it contains only standard variable definitions and function declarations (build/package), downloads a pinned GitHub release with SHA-512 checksum verification, and uses standard `zig build` commands. The package step installs built files and generates shell completions by running the freshly built binary—a normal pattern. No malicious injections, suspicious network requests, or unexpected system modifications are present.
data.disagreement_analysis: Report 1 encountered an API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) during detailed PKGBUILD review, resulting in an inconclusive verdict. Report 2 successfully reviewed the same PKGBUILD and found it safe. The disagreement is technical (tool failure) rather than substantive.
coverage_issues: Report 1 failed to complete detailed PKGBUILD review due to API error
learnings: When a model encounters a tool error on a critical file like PKGBUILD, the audit should either retry the request or escalate to a different model rather than marking the entire audit inconclusive
Initial PKGBUILD audits that succeed should be weighted more heavily when detailed reviews fail due to transient errors
Tool errors should be distinguished from substantive security disagreements in the verdict aggregation logic
